input.rationale: Queuing the probe built and locally verified for the child admission question's registered discriminator. It measures the two remaining halves: whether the node with an empty configuration campaigns on its own, and whether it accepts an outsider's AppendEntries and takes that non-member as its leader. A setup event was added so the setup and the results are separate emissions.

scope.description: A single-node in-memory cluster with a commit-tracking store and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled is restarted from its own stores so its configuration is empty; the node is then watched over several heartbeat timeouts for any campaign of its own, after which an outsider reachable through the transport sends one AppendEntries request with a higher term and no entries, and the node's state, its leader identity and the response are recorded.
assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration so the restarted node's configuration is empty rather than stale.
The outsider is a server that appears in no configuration the node holds; it is wired to the node's transport for the duration of the probe.
The AppendEntries request carries no entries, so accepting it only means accepting the sender as leader.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, apply five commands, shut the node down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and emit the setup event with the live configuration length and whether the node is in its own configuration; sleep six heartbeat timeouts and record the node's state and any leader it knows; wire an outsider transport, send AppendEntries from the outsider with term+1, no entries and commit index 0, then emit the result event with the response success, the response term, the leader the node now reports and whether the outsider became that leader.
experiment.requirement: A node that recovers from its own log must not accept a server outside the configuration it recorded as its leader, and its own election gating must stay consistent with the configuration it holds.
experiment.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose leadership to record and the follower loop decides when the node campaigns, both from the configuration the node recovered.

comparisons.description: A server outside the node's configuration does not become the node's leader.
The node does not start an election of its own while its configuration is empty.

scope.description: Two restart scenarios on a single-node in-memory cluster created by the repository's own MakeClusterCustom helper, whose log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore and whose Config sets RestoreCommittedLogs=true. Each scenario commits entries, restarts the node from its retained log/stable/snapshot stores with a fresh in-memory transport via NewRaft, and reports the recovered commit index, lastApplied, the scan start index, whether a committed configuration entry is inside the scanned range, and the node's latest configuration before and after restart.
assumptions: The CommitTrackingLogStore implementation is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore.
The transport is the repository's InmemTransport and the FSM is the repository's MockFSM.
RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, as documented in config.go.
No fault injection, no artificial delays and no modification of production logic.

basis.prefix: Scenario A (event restore_committed_logs_no_snapshot): bootstrap a one-node cluster whose first log entry is a committed LogConfiguration, apply ten commands (all committed, no snapshot exists), sample the store's GetCommitIndex and the latest configuration, then Shutdown and restart with NewRaft from the same stores. Scenario B (event restore_committed_logs_snapshot_and_config_change): apply twenty commands, take a user snapshot, commit AddNonvoter(nonvoter-B), apply ten more commands so the commit-tracking store stages a commit index beyond the configuration entry, then Shutdown and restart the same way.
basis.requirement: On restart, a node's configuration state (used for participant eligibility, election gating and quorum) must include every configuration entry its log store reports as committed, including entries at or below the recovered commit index.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft owns loading the node's configuration from its log and snapshot history, and the RestoreCommittedLogs option must not leave that state behind the committed history.

scope.description: Two single-node in-memory clusters (repository MakeClusterCustom, CommitTrackingLogStore, RestoreCommittedLogs=true, snapshotting disabled) commit different amounts of authored history, then restart via NewRaft in a goroutine with a bounded wait: 6000 commands as a control (94 batches of 64) and 9000 commands (141 batches). Each case emits a setup event and one result event stating whether NewRaft returned, and, if not, the blocked goroutine frames captured with runtime.Stack.
assumptions: The log store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore and the transport the repository's InmemTransport.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration so the recovered range starts at index 0 with no snapshot.
Only the amount of committed history differs between the two cases; the same harness, helper and configuration are used.
No test is expected to block the whole package run: the restart is wrapped in a bounded select.

basis.prefix: For each case: bootstrap a one-node cluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, apply N commands to completion, record the staged commit index and the derived batch count, Shutdown, restart with NewRaft from the same stores inside a goroutine and wait up to 20 seconds; on return report lastApplied, commit index and configuration length after restart, otherwise report the observed wait and the frames of every goroutine containing github.com/hashicorp/raft plus chan-send/select markers.
basis.requirement: NewRaft must complete its startup recovery for any legal retained state; RestoreCommittedLogs must not leave the node unable to finish construction when the recovered committed range is large.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: NewRaft owns recovery ordering, including when the FSM consumer goroutine starts relative to the recovery work it feeds.

comparisons.description: The control range (fewer batches than the fsmMutateCh capacity) completes startup recovery.
The range exceeding the fsmMutateCh batch capacity also completes startup recovery.

scope.description: One single-node in-memory cluster (repository MakeClusterCustom, CommitTrackingLogStore, RestoreCommittedLogs=true, snapshotting disabled) commits ten commands, restarts via NewRaft so its configuration is empty, and then receives a RequestVote and a RequestPreVote over a real in-memory transport from a candidate whose ID appears in no configuration. The harness emits one setup event with the log-recorded and live configuration sizes and one result event with the two responses, the derived quorum size and the candidate's membership.
assumptions: The log store is the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore; the candidate transport is the repository's InmemTransport wired to the restarted node's transport.
The candidate's log is up to date and its term is higher than the restarted node's term, so no log-recency or term rule rejects it by itself.
The node's log-recorded configuration (the bootstrapped LogConfiguration at index 1) is the cluster membership in force; the empty live configuration comes from the node's own recovery path.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, apply ten commands, record the log-recorded configuration, Shutdown, restart with NewRaft from the same stores, emit the setup event (log_recorded_config_len, live_config_len, live_voters, derived_quorum_size), then send RequestVote and RequestPreVote through the transport path with candidate ID 'outsider-not-in-log' and emit the responses.
basis.requirement: A node whose configuration is in force (recorded in its own log) must treat vote and pre-vote requests from servers outside that configuration as non-members, and its quorum accounting must follow that configuration.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration state is produced by its own restart recovery, and the admission rules in requestVote/requestPreVote rely on it being populated.

comparisons.description: A candidate that is not in the configuration recorded in the node's log is not granted a vote.
The same candidate is not granted a pre-vote.

scope.description: One five-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled. Two voters are removed so the configuration in force is a three-voter set, the node under test snapshots in that state, the two voters are re-added, later traffic is committed, and the node is restarted from its retained stores. Its stub configuration and the peers it replicates to are recorded, leadership is transferred to it, the write it acknowledges is recorded together with the nodes that hold it, every holder is shut down, and the leader elected afterwards is checked for the acknowledged write.
assumptions: Transports are the repository's InmemTransport, log stores the repository's InmemCommitTrackingStore, the FSM is the repository's MockFSM, and configuration changes use the public AddVoter/RemoveServer APIs.
ShutdownOnRemove is false so that removing a voter that happens to be the leader does not terminate the process under test.
Only transport-level disconnection is used to isolate a peer; no fault is injected into any node's logic.
The payload check reads each node's log store for the exact byte payload.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap five voters with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs=true; RemoveServer the two voters that will later be re-added; apply a few commands so the FSM can snapshot; take a user snapshot on the node under test while the three-voter configuration is committed; AddVoter both nodes again; apply twenty traffic commands so the node's staged commit index passes the recommitted entries; capture its configuration, shut it down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and rewire the transports; record the live configuration, staged commit index, last applied, and whether the log still holds a configuration entry beyond the snapshot; transfer leadership to the restarted node and wait until it reports Leader; disconnect it from one voter; apply the payload; record each node's possession of the payload, the derived quorums and whether the write was backed by a true majority; shut down every holder; wait for a leader among the survivors and record whether it holds the acknowledged payload.
basis.requirement: An entry that a leader acknowledges to a client must be stored by a majority of the configuration in force at the time, and must be present in the log of any leader later elected from that configuration.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the leader's commit rule and quorum accounting use the configuration the node recovered, and the node's own recovery path is what leaves that configuration behind the log's committed history.

comparisons.description: The write the stale-configuration leader acknowledges is held by at least a majority of the five-voter configuration in force.
The acknowledged write survives in the leader elected from the configuration in force.

scope.description: A two-voter in-memory cluster applies three commands, commits an AddNonvoter configuration change, and then reports that change's own index, the index from the public configuration future, the documented stats key, and the live configuration, together with the log entry type at the change's index.
assumptions: The cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own test facilities (MakeClusterCustom with InmemTransport and MockFSM).
The configuration change is committed because its future returned without error, which is the premise for the index comparison.
No internal state is required for the comparison: the change index comes from its public future, the endpoints come from public methods, and the log entry type comes from the log store.

basis.prefix: Start a two-peer cluster, apply three commands to completion, commit AddNonvoter for a new server, emit the setup event with the change index, the entry type at that index and the peer count, then call GetConfiguration() and Stats() and emit the future index, the stats value, both derived match booleans and the live configuration.
basis.requirement: The configuration future returned to a client, and the documented latest_configuration_index stat, must report the index of the configuration entry in force rather than a constant.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: both endpoints are produced inside the library from the configuration it already tracks.

comparisons.description: The index reported by the public configuration future equals the committed configuration entry's index.
The documented latest_configuration_index stat equals the committed configuration entry's index.

scope.description: A two-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking stores and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: the follower is restarted from its own stores so its configuration is empty, then the serving leader commits a new configuration entry (AddNonvoter) and the restarted node's configuration is read before and after that entry arrives.
assumptions: Transports, log stores and FSM are the repository's own InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration, so the restarted node has no snapshot and its configuration is empty rather than stale.
The restarted node remains in the serving leader's configuration, so the new configuration entry is replicated to it as a new entry.

basis.prefix: Start a two-peer cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores; apply five commands; record the follower's configuration and the configuration entry recorded in its log at index 1; shut the follower down and restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport, then rewire all transports; emit the setup event with the configuration before the restart, the log-recorded configuration and the live configuration length after the restart; commit AddNonvoter on the serving leader; wait until the restarted node reports a non-empty configuration and emit the result event with the change index and type and the repaired configuration.
basis.requirement: A node that restarted with an empty or stale configuration must regain the configuration in force once the cluster replicates a configuration entry to it.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the node's configuration is loaded by its own recovery and updated by the entries it receives.

comparisons.description: A configuration entry committed after the restart restores the node's configuration to the configuration in force.

scope.description: A three-voter in-memory cluster with a serving leader: one follower is removed with RemoveServer, the removed node is allowed to receive the entry that drops it from the configuration, and then that removed node sends a TimeoutNow request over the transport to the remaining follower while the leader is healthy. The probe records the configuration in force, the removed node's membership, the target's state and term before and after, the serving leader's state, and who leads afterwards.
assumptions: Cluster, transports and FSM are the repository's own MakeCluster, InmemTransport and MockFSM facilities, and the removal uses the public RemoveServer API.
The removed node stays transport-reachable, which is the situation for a server that has been taken out of the configuration but not shut down.
The request is delivered through the same transport method the library uses for leadership transfer.

basis.prefix: Start a three-voter cluster, wait for a leader and commit one command; choose a follower to remove and another follower as target; RemoveServer the first one and wait until the removed node's own configuration no longer contains it; emit the setup event with the configuration in force, the removed node's membership, the target's state and term, and the leader; send TimeoutNow from the removed node's transport to the target, wait until the target is leader or leadership changes, then emit the result event with the timeout error, the target's state and term, the old leader's state and whether it stepped down, whether a leader is present afterwards and whether the target became it.
basis.requirement: Only the current leader of the configuration in force may trigger a leadership transfer; a server outside that configuration must not be able to make a voter campaign or to displace the serving leader.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the TimeoutNow handler decides what a received transfer trigger means, and the vote handler decides how much trust to extend to a transfer-flagged campaign.

comparisons.description: A server outside the configuration in force cannot change who leads.
The serving leader keeps its authority when a non-member sends a transfer trigger.

basis.requirement: Only the current leader of the configuration in force may trigger a leadership transfer; a server outside that configuration must not be able to make a voter campaign or to displace the serving leader.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: the TimeoutNow handler decides what a received transfer trigger means, and the vote handler decides how much trust to extend to a transfer-flagged campaign.

The serving leader keeps its authority when a non-member sends a transfer trigger.

result.summary: Queued the remaining half of the child admission question: a new harness case (setup event plus result event) that restarts a node with an empty configuration, watches it over several heartbeat timeouts, and then sends an outsider's AppendEntries to see whether that non-member becomes the node's leader; locally the node stayed Follower and did not campaign on its own, yet accepted the outsider as leader with the response marking success. The experiment is now requested against the fixed snapshot, with a source range covering runFollower added so the election-gating anchor verifies. That receipt is unread, so the question's account still rests on the earlier vote and pre-vote evidence.

assumptions: Cluster, transport, log store and FSM are the repository's own MakeClusterCustom, InmemTransport, InmemCommitTrackingStore and MockFSM facilities.
Snapshotting is disabled by configuration so the restarted node's configuration is empty rather than stale.
The outsider is a server that appears in no configuration the node holds; it is wired to the node's transport for the duration of the probe.
The AppendEntries request carries no entries, so accepting it only means accepting the sender as leader.

basis.prefix: Bootstrap a one-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs and commit-tracking stores, apply five commands, shut the node down, restart it with NewRaft on a fresh transport and emit the setup event with the live configuration length and whether the node is in its own configuration; sleep six heartbeat timeouts and record the node's state and any leader it knows; wire an outsider transport, send AppendEntries from the outsider with term+1, no entries and commit index 0, then emit the result event with the response success, the response term, the leader the node now reports and whether the outsider became that leader.
basis.requirement: A node that recovers from its own log must not accept a server outside the configuration it recorded as its leader, and its own election gating must stay consistent with the configuration it holds.
basis.responsibility: Raft itself: appendEntries decides whose leadership to record and the follower loop decides when the node campaigns, both from the configuration the node recovered.

comparisons.description: A server outside the node's configuration does not become the node's leader.
The node does not start an election of its own while its configuration is empty.
